stories.headline: Decade-long efforts averted energy crisis during war: PM Narendra Modi
stories.title: Decade-long efforts averted energy crisis during war: PM Narendra Modi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said steps taken in the last decade helped the country to sail through the crisis emerged during the war in the Middle East. He was inaugurating various welfare projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore here, including renewable energy and petroleum infrastructure. "War around Iran and Gulf countries shows how important energy security is. Steps taken for energy security in the last decade helped the country face the crisis with resilience," the PM said. Regarding the Metro Pink Line, which was dedicated to the public, Modi said it gives better connectivity to people in Bengaluru. He also noted that the Metro rail network increased from 17 km in 2014 to over 100 km in 2026 in Bengaluru. On the occasion, Modi lauded Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav for serving the nation as the widow of a Kargil war hero.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu opposes ASI control of Thirupparankundram temple in Supreme Court
stories.title: Tamil Nadu opposes ASI control of Thirupparankundram temple in Supreme Court
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu opposes ASI control of Thirupparankundram temple in Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The dispute concerns where and by whom the sacred lamp should be lit on the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai.
For decades, the lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes.

The Tamil Nadu government has strongly opposed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking Archaeological Survey of India control over the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and Thirupparankundram hill, along with changes to the traditional Karthigai Deepam celebrations, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
Hindu groups have sought permission to light it at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone lamp pillar higher up the hill and about 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya dargah.
In an affidavit filed before a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department opposed the petition.
It said ownership of the temple and existing religious practices had been settled through decades of court proceedings.
HR&CE Commissioner TG Vinay said the hill is owned by the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple to the extent recognised by a civil court decree in 1923, which was restored by the Privy Council in 1931.

The Hindu Dharma Parishad has sought three directions: handing over the entire temple and hill to the ASI, keeping a lamp burning round the clock at the stone pillar described as the Deepathoon, and illuminating the entire hill with lamps during Karthigai Deepam.

According to PTI, the affidavit said: "A title so settled cannot be disturbed, and the administration of a religious endowment entrusted by statute to the HR&CE cannot be wrested away and handed over to the ASI upon a petition that pleads no ground in law and seeks the relief in the teeth of a concluded civil adjudication of title."

It added: "The department is the statutory custodian and administrator of the temple, and have at all times protected the temple, its properties and the rights of its devotees, including by asserting and defending the title of the temple in the civil courts over the course of a century, by conducting the worship and the festivals of the temple in accordance with the Agamas, and by making every arrangement for the smooth and peaceful conduct of the Karthigai Deepam each year in consultation with the police, fire and revenue authorities."

On the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam, the commissioner said the festival lamp had traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple, and not at the hilltop or the stone pillar now described as the Deepathoon.
The affidavit said the practice had continued for more than 150 years in accordance with the Agamas and the opinion of the temple's Sthanikars, or traditional functionaries.

stories.headline: Keralam sanctions ₹20.52 crore to clear pending CM Kids Scholarship dues ahead of Children's Day
stories.title: Keralam sanctions ₹20.52 crore to clear pending CM Kids Scholarship dues ahead of Children's Day
stories.summary: Kerala has sanctioned ₹20.52 crore to clear pending CM Kids Scholarship arrears for LSS and USS students, with Chief Minister VD Satheesan directing urgent disbursement to eligible beneficiaries by March 31.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Thiruvananthapuram: The government has sanctioned ₹20.52 crore to clear the pending arrears under the CM Kids Scholarship scheme for students who qualified in the Lower Secondary Scholarship (LSS) and Upper Secondary Scholarship (USS) examinations.
Chief Minister VD Satheesan has directed the Additional Chief Secretary of the Finance Department to urgently allocate the amount for disbursing the pending scholarships.
The decision follows a request from the General Education Department.
The scholarship amount for the current academic year (2026-27) will be disbursed by March 31, the Chief Minister's Office said in a press release on Friday.
The Chief Minister has instructed the departments concerned to ensure that all eligible students receive the scholarship within the stipulated timeframe.
He has also directed officials to streamline the procedures to prevent scholarship payments from piling up as arrears in the future.
The government described the decision as a Children's Day gift to students.
